text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Manchester City and Nottingham Forest at the Etihad Stadium.

After claiming a historic treble last season, the Citizens have started this term in similarly impressive fashion, taking victories in all five of their Premier League outings while coming from behind to beat Red Star Belgrade in the Champions League in midweek.
Another league win here will boost their chances of lifting a sixth title in the space of seven campaigns.

The visitors may have narrowly avoided relegation last season, but they have fared well in the early stages of this one, currently sitting in the top eight of the Premier League having taken seven points from their first five matches.
They are right up against it here, though, with the 6-0 hammering they suffered here last campaign sure to be playing on the mind of the Forest squad.

Pep Guardiola makes three changes from the 3-1 win over Red Star as Akanji and Gvardiol replace Ake and Gomez in the back four while Doku comes in for Bernardo Silva, who picked up a knock in that game and joins an already busy physio room that includes the likes of Kevin De Bruyne, Mateo Kovacic and John Stones.
Guardiola is boosted by the return of Grealish, though, as the winger is fit enough to be named on the bench.
Steve Cooper makes five alterations from the 1-1 draw with Burnley last time out.
Hudson-Odoi scored a brilliant equaliser in that game, but he drops to the bench alongside Elanga as Tavares and Dominguez come in.
Boly, Niakhate and Aurier also start ahead of Montiel, Worrall and Scott McKenna, the latter of whom misses out altogether.
The two teams make their way onto the pitch at the Etihad Stadium and we are now moments from kick-off.
The hosts kick us off and we are under way in sunny Manchester!
Haaland is hauled down by Boly near the edge of the box as Alvarez looked to play him in, and City will have a free-kick in a great shooting position.
Alvarez scored directly from a free-kick against Red Star in midweek, but his powerful effort is beaten away by Turner on this occasion.
Forest are playing with 10 of their players behind the ball, trying to fill the spaces that City are such experts at exploiting.
GOAL!!! FODEN PUTS CITY AHEAD!!! It all comes from a sublime Rodri pass, as he lofts a brilliant throughball over the top for Walker.
The right-back takes it in his stride before teeing up Foden, who shows all of his great technique to blast into the bottom corner and give the hosts a 1-0 lead!
Walker's assist was perfectly weighted for Foden to thump home.
City have now scored in their last 36 Premier League home games.
It already looks like it could be a long remainder of this game for Forest, who are struggling to get out of their own half at the moment.
Awoniyi is looking pretty isolated up top for the visitors.
Walker gets to the byline before trying to find Haaland with a cross, though Boly is well-placed to divert behind for a corner, which then comes to nothing.
GOAL!!! HAALAND MAKES IT 2-0!!! Tavares gives the ball away in a dangerous position and City take full advantage.
Foden plays a clever pass through to Nunes, who lofts a sublime delivery to the back post for Haaland.
In typically ruthless fashion, the Norway international powers home his header, giving Turner no chance to put his team 2-0 up!
Nunes' cross found Haaland in space before the City forward thundered home his header.
Haaland has now scored in his last four games in the Premier League (six goals in total)
Akanji goes in the book for bringing down Awoniyi.
Perhaps more pressing, though, is that Forest will have a free-kick in a dangerous position.
Who will be trusted to take it?
After a lengthy delay, Gibbs-White's free-kick is not worth the wait as it hits the wall.
The ball does deflect behind for a corner, but City deal with that with ease.
Tavares is booked for cynically bringing down Doku as City looked to counter.

There were 46 passes in the build-up to Foden's opener, the second most on record (since 2006-07) in a Premier League game after 48 passes in the build-up to Nacer Chadli’s goal for Tottenham against QPR in August 2014.
Space opens up for Alvarez to smash towards goal, but his powerful effort is straight down the throat of Turner and the Forest goalkeeper makes the save.
Haaland already has eight Premier League goals this season, racking up another strike on his sixth appearance of 2023-24 versus Forest here.
However, his first six Premier League appearances last season saw him score 10, so he is still behind that extraordinary scoring rate.
City nearly have a third as Doku shows quick feet to skip past Aina before finding Alvarez, but the Argentina international's eventual effort is blocked behind for a corner by Boly.
City are unbeaten in six league games against Forest (four wins, two draws) since a 3-2 home defeat in the second tier in December 1997, and that run looks like it will be extended to seven here.
Cooper may be forced into a change here with Tavares down and clutching his groin.
He looks in some discomfort.
Tavares is going to try and play on, though he does not look to be moving entirely freely.
Can City take advantage of that?
He bravely tried to play on, but Tavares' race finally looks run as he goes down again.
Tavares does indeed limp off, and Montiel comes on to replace him.
Forest players are left fuming as Aurier is penalised for going through the back of Doku around 30 yards out from their goal.
There will be further outrage if Alvarez can find the back of the net with the resulting free-kick.
Alvarez's free-kick is blocked by Boly in the wall, though the hosts will have another chance to score a third as Foden heads over to take a corner.
Foden takes the set-piece short to Alvarez, but the substitute Montiel is alert to race out and snuff out the danger by forcing City backwards.
There will be five minutes of additional time at the end of this first half.
Sangare is booked for a late challenge on Rodri in midfield.
Forest are yet to have a shot on target in this game.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 2-0 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
City are in control as they take a 2-0 lead into the break at the Etihad Stadium thanks to goals from Foden and Haaland.
The hosts were ahead after just seven minutes, Rodri's excellent lofted pass unlocking the Forest defence before Walker teed up Foden to lash into the bottom corner.
Turner also had no chance as Haaland doubled City's lead after 14 minutes, Foden again playing a big part as he played in Nunes, who lofted a deft cross over for Haaland to nod home.

The visitors must have been dreading the rest of the opening 45 minutes, though they did manage to restrict the Citizens to just the two first-half goals and give themselves a slender chance of a comeback after the interval.
City are imperious at home, last dropping points at the Etihad Stadium on New Year's Eve in 2022, when they were held to a 1-1 draw by Everton.

It will be interesting to see whether Cooper looks to take risks in the chance of a surprise come-from-behind result, or whether he will opt to shut up shop and protect his team from the same kind of damaging defeat they suffered here last season.
Cooper's side get us back under way for the second period.
CITY ARE DOWN TO 10!! Rodri and Gibbs-White clash in the corner, and the City midfielder appears to grab at his throat, sending the Forest man tumbling to the turf.
The referee sprints over to separate the pair, before brandishing a red card to Rodri.
There will be a VAR check, though, to rule whether the sending-off will stand...
Gibbs-White sees yellow for his part in the fracas.

RODRI IS OFF!!! The VAR review agrees with the referee's initial decision to send the midfielder off, and he is forced to make his way from the field! That was very naive from such an experienced player.
City seemed to be in complete control before that incident.
How will Forest look to press home their numerical advantage?
The visitors work a corner short before the ball ends up at the feet of Mangala outside the box, but the midfielder's shot is ballooned high over the crossbar.
Doku is the man Guardiola chooses to sacrifice as Phillips comes on to fill the gap created by Rodri's dismissal.
Forest’s first completed pass came after seven minutes and 36 seconds in the first half.
Prior to City's opener, the visitors had had just six touches.
Aina flies past Walker down the left, forcing Akanji to come and clear behind for a corner.
Cooper's men look like they have been revitalised by the red card.
Cooper looks to his bench, bringing on Elanga for Sangare.
In another attacking change, Hudson-Odoi comes on for Aurier.
Can the former Chelsea man replicate the heroics he produced against Burnley?
Alvarez is replaced by Ake.
A superb long ball from Boly puts Awoniyi in, but he is quickly closed down by Ederson and the Forest striker can only loft high over the crossbar.
There was a bit of a melee between Ederson and Awoniyi after that missed opportunity, with the City goalkeeper unhappy with his opponent for trying to win a penalty.
The Brazil international is booked for the incident.
Awoniyi also sees yellow.
This is just Forest's third visit to the Etihad Stadium to face City – they won an FA Cup tie 3-0 in January 2009, before losing this exact fixture 6-0 in August last season.
Dominguez tries to curl home from range, but he cannot get enough bend on his effort and Ederson watches it fly well wide of his post.
Foden flies past Boly like the Forest defender is not even there.
He gets all the way into the visitors' box, but his attempt to cross for Haaland is blocked behind by Montiel.
After having just 23.4 per cent of the possession in the first half, Cooper's men have had 72.1 per cent of the ball since the break.
They are yet to really trouble City though.
If the visitors are to find a way back into this game, they will have to provide more attacking threat having not been able to record a shot on target so far.
Elanga tries to arrow a cross towards the back post for Awoniyi, but the delivery fails to find its desired target and City will have a goal-kick.
Gvardiol can only nod a cross to the waiting Elanga at the back post, but the substitute's shot is easily saved by Ederson.
Forest are getting closer.
Rodri's sending off (45 minutes and 27 seconds) was the fastest red card shown from the start of a second half on record in the Premier League (since 2006-07).
Cooper is gambling as he brings on two strikers.
Origi enters the fray in place of Aina.
Wood is on to replace Awoniyi.
Mangala catches Foden in midfield and receives a yellow card for his troubles.
A great chance for City to kill the game goes begging as Ake gets on the end of a diagonal free-kick.
The substitute manages to get the ball across to Haaland, but the pass is at an awkward height for the prolific forward and he can only fire over the crossbar.
Will the hosts regret that miss come full-time?
With 10 minutes to play, City still hold a two-goal advantage, though they have looked a little nervy since Rodri's red card.
Origi is booked after his high boot catches Gvardiol as the pair battled for an aerial ball.
Gvardiol required a bit of treatment after the foul on him, though he is now back on his feet and okay to continue.
Space opens up for Origi to smash goalwards, but a couple of City defenders are there to block the striker's effort away from danger.
Grealish returns from injury to make his first appearance since late August, coming on for Foden.
There is a brief moment of concern for the hosts as a clearance in their box comes off Elanga and flies goalwards, though thankfully for them, the ball smashes into the side netting.
The fourth official puts up his board and indicates there will be seven minutes of additional time at the end of this match.
Can Forest set up a grandstand finish?
Gibbs-White whips a free-kick into the hosts' box, but the ball somehow evades everybody before skimming away harmlessly for a throw-in.
There is another flashpoint as Montiel clashes with Grealish near the touchline, for which the Forest man receives a yellow card.
Grealish also goes in the book.
Ederson makes a brilliant save to palm Elanga's full-blooded effort away, then makes another decent stop to deny Boly from range.
Ederson takes the pressure off his defenders as he comes out and claims a cross from the left.
City are nearly there.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 2-0 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
The full-time whistle blows as City take the points in an occasionally ill-tempered clash at the Etihad Stadium.
They run out 2-0 victors, set on their way by Foden's fine finish in just the seventh minute after Rodri's superb pass had carved open the Forest defence.
Haaland made it 2-0 shortly after, thumping home a header from Nunes' deft cross as the visitors made it to the break just the two goals behind.
They were then handed a lifeline just 27 seconds into the second half, their hosts reduced to 10 men with Rodri given his marching orders for grabbing the throat of Gibbs-White.
Cooper's side failed to make their numerical advantage count, though, and City saw out the remaining minutes with relative ease to secure another win.
With most of their challengers at the top yet to play this weekend, City extend their lead at the Premier League summit to five points as they retain their perfect record to kick off this campaign.
They face Newcastle United in EFL Cup action next, the only competition they failed to win last season.

For Forest, whether they stay up will not be dictated by games against the likes of City and Cooper will find some pleasure in how his team did not crumble in the same manner they did in this fixture last season.
They host Brentford in their next match on October 1.
Thanks for joining us for live coverage of Manchester City's 2-0 Premier League victory over Nottingham Forest at the Etihad Stadium.
Goodbye!
